name: adult screening overview
title: Adult screening decision chart for a healthy adult at a periodic health encounter: smoking and lung cancer, lipids and diabetes by age and risk, then the average-risk cancer programs (colorectal, breast, cervical) with who is in, the test and interval, and who leaves for a high-risk route; abdominal aortic aneurysm and bone density from 65, no routine PSA

root.title: Healthy adult at a periodic health encounter (PHE): WHAT do I screen for, WHEN, and with WHAT?
lines: stable (airway, breathing, circulation + vitals) → history: risk factors → exam: body mass index (BMI), blood pressure (BP), heart rate
tests chosen by RISK, not a fixed panel: will the result CHANGE MANAGEMENT? (Choosing Wisely)
screen with a very SENSITIVE test (negative rules OUT), confirm with a very SPECIFIC one (positive rules IN)

groups.title: RISK FACTORS + CHRONIC DISEASE
lines: by age, earlier if at higher risk
from 65: bone density, aortic aneurysm → see the OLDER ADULT chart

groups.title: CANCER: AVERAGE risk and NO symptoms?
lines: yes → the program below · symptoms or HIGH risk → out of it (red / amber boxes)

pres.title: Ask at every PHE
lines: • poverty: "trouble making ends meet at the end of the month?"
• alcohol + drugs · mood + stressors: see the ANXIETY AND STRESS chart
• exercise + diet: SEDENTARISM is always a risk; BMI alone is not

pres.title: Programs for the ASYMPTOMATIC only
lines: • high risk → its own route, earlier or more often
• prostate: NO routine prostate-specific antigen (PSA) · shared decision from 40 if Black or family history

head: h
Smoking + lung cancer
ask every adult
next: • Ask, Advise to quit, Assess readiness
• Arrange follow-up ≤ 1 week after quit date

head: h
Lipids
high cholesterol → heart disease, stroke
who: ~earlier if higher risk: diabetes, some ethnic groups

head: h
Type 2 diabetes
next: At risk or PREDIABETES → rescreen MORE OFTEN

head: h
Colorectal cancer (CRC)
next: • prior CRC or adenomatous polyps, inflammatory bowel disease
• family: start 10 years before a 1st-degree relative's age at diagnosis

head: h
Breast cancer
next: • BRCA1/2 or other mutation, or a carrier's 1st-degree relative
• personal/family breast or ovarian cancer, chest radiation < 30

head: h
Cervical cancer
who: Age ≥ 25, has a cervix, EVER sexually active
test: cervical swab for high-risk types: replaced the Pap test
next: A positive result: see the CERVICAL SCREENING chart
